title: Persona Dream Kling E2E acceptance path
question: Walk me through the Persona Dream Embry/Horus Kling E2E from idea to voiced discussion.
teleprompter_points: The public acceptance path starts from one human dream idea and preserves it as lineage through the Kling smoke, journal, and conversation receipts.
The E2E driver now requests three reference-bound Kling clips by default, then assembles them before the journal and Chatterbox conversation run.
The proof boundary is explicit: this is a direct Kling smoke, not proof of the canonical scene-table/create-kling-scene compiler path.
proof_boundary: Live paid Kling proof requires explicit provider authorization and successful agentic-evals receipt; dry-run and cinematography-only cases prove gating, not live provider return.

debugger_stops.proves: The E2E driver validates cinematography coverage before provider requests are built.

related_questions: Where does paid provider authorization enter?

steps.title: Idea and provider smoke
bullets: The human idea is recorded before any provider work.
The Kling request is direct and marked canonical_compiler=false.
Reference assets are uploaded and hash-read before submit.
steps.source_explanation: main() writes idea lineage, reference receipts, direct request validation, clip responses, and assembled video proof.
steps.proof_boundary: Provider return is live only when the agentic eval live case passes.

steps.title: Journal and voiced discussion
bullets: The assembled video is bound into dream_packet.json.
Embry's journal is rendered through Chatterbox.
The Horus/Embry discussion must produce audio-backed conversation turns.
steps.source_explanation: The same E2E command writes dream_journal.v1.json, journal.wav, conversation.jsonl, and dynamic_conversation_receipt.v1.json.
steps.proof_boundary: Chatterbox receipts prove rendering and file hashes, not human perception.

title: Default cinematography coverage for dialogue video plans
question: How does Persona Dream prevent static two-shot dialogue clips when the speaker changes?
teleprompter_points: Dialogue video plans now emit cinematography_coverage_receipt.json by default before storyboard prompts can feed provider planning.
Each speaking beat has speaker, coverage, camera, eyeline, and matched framing fields; the first three beats alternate Embry, Horus, Embry.
Diarization ownership stays external: Persona Dream consumes Watch pyannote receipts after audio is muxed; Live Evidence speaker turns are not diarization.
proof_boundary: Coverage receipts prove planned shot grammar and named post-audio verification ownership; visual speaker framing still requires rendered-clip review, and diarization requires muxed audio through Watch.

debugger_stops.proves: The default video_plan builder constructs the coverage receipt from speaker-specific shot specs, not from free prose.

command: Horus and Embry have tea under a patio umbrella on a void world.

related_questions: Why is Watch the diarization owner?

steps.title: Coverage is default pipeline state
bullets: The video_plan builder creates shot_specs with speaker-specific coverage.
The receipt names best-practices-cinematography and records stable eyelines.
The generated storyboard, timed transcript, and prompts copy speaker/coverage fields.
steps.source_explanation: _build_video_plan creates cinematography_coverage and writes speaker/coverage/eyeline into the downstream artifacts.
steps.proof_boundary: This proves planning grammar, not generated pixel quality.

steps.title: Diarization remains Watch-owned
bullets: Persona Dream says post-mux who-spoke-when requires Watch pyannote.
Live Evidence can supply live speaker-turn transcript events.
Live Evidence is not treated as the diarization authority.
steps.source_explanation: SKILL.md defines the ownership boundary so the pipeline does not invent a second diarizer.
steps.proof_boundary: Watch pyannote must still run on a muxed audio/video artifact before claiming acoustic speaker timing.
